lead: The modelling section calls the plant cold-tolerant and wide-dispersing without direct physiological evidence, and its whole-plant reconstruction is conjectural. Later valve and dehiscence interpretations depend partly on sources not read directly.

The axis-diameter maximum comes from an unreviewed web resource and was not checked against the primary description. The spore-output figure is calculated. Lyonophyton denotes the associated gametophyte generation, not a congener supplying a borrowed trait.

The card alternates between total-group and crown-embryophyte interpretations of trilete spores. Cooksonia traits occur in explanatory notes, while the corresponding front-matter states remain unknown; they are not assigned as traits of the Ordovician producers.

The card flags a conflict between a Late Cretaceous earliest-fossil statement and its 118.56 Ma calibration. The sequential culture timings are not reconciled with the separately reported 3-month complete cycle. Mixed-genus experimental results require species-specific attribution.

The front-matter minimum height is 1100 cm, while its note gives 11.2-31.5 m. Heterospory is called demonstrated despite inferred megaspore association. Post-burial resprouting becomes categorical in the modelling section although the anatomical discussion calls it plausible.

The modelling section states that mycorrhiza was absent and uptake probably poorer, whereas the physiological discussion leaves uptake unresolved. Better-drained habitat is inferred from preservation. The reconstructed body does not yet establish connections to every orthotropic and fertile axis.

The stated Pridoli interval 422.7-419.62 Ma does not overlap the quoted crown-tracheophyte estimate 432-428 Ma, despite the card's overlap claim. The 2017 description and the reported challenge to the fossil's identity were not read directly.

The height field encodes preserved length as stature. The diameter maximum depends on an unseen thesis. Leaf state records the most advanced member rather than the assemblage's modal condition. Lochkovian is a conservative baseline, not a directly demonstrated first occurrence.

The front matter ends the range in the Pragian although its notes include Emsian formation ages. Congener comparisons leave branching and stomata unknown; they do not supply transferred front-matter values. Primary descriptions were not read in full.

The body says no in situ spores are reported, but the front matter records immature spores in a Macivera sporangium. The height maximum encodes an incomplete preserved length. Assemblage homospory is supported only by the Macivera diagnosis.

The genus-labelled card explicitly covers the class, so class summaries lack species-level provenance. Gorstian is an unresolved older bound within the Ludlow record; the Pragian Charales assignment is also questioned. Culture outcomes are not apportioned between the two C. braunii strains.

The desiccation study's two species are unnamed, preventing species-specific calibration. Zygote nuclear divisions are disputed; the card alternates zoospore and meiospore terminology. Zygote provisioning is asserted, while transport across the putative transfer cells remains an open question.

The supplement's "560 mm" holotype length is flagged as a typo. The nominal height field stores fragment lengths. Detrital-zircon ages are maxima, and the stated Lochkovian last record conflicts with an older claim extending the genus through the Lower Devonian.

Halle's diagnosis is quoted through a registry; the Oxfordshire description was read only as an abstract. Røragen has no resolved modern stage. Some geographically extensive records are unchecked, and the PBDB locality tally is awkwardly worded.

The species concept and long range may combine several taxa; Givetian is a project truncation. Stomatal type is disputed, and the G-type tracheid label comes from a secondary summary. The congener's stomatal subtype is compared rather than required to establish presence; rooting provenance is identified elsewhere in the card.

The front matter spells Horneophyton ligneri, whereas the body uses lignieri. The general claim that Rhynie hosts were rootless sits alongside a root-bearing Asteroxylon counter-example. The Ordovician age/identity and the quoted numerical versus stage ages remain explicitly uncertain.
resolution: 'ligneri' is the spelling in the title of Strullu-Derrien et al. (2014); the citation is correct

lead: Group front-matter states conceal member variation: microphylls include avascular enations, and G-type tracheids are verified only for Asteroxylon. Recovered sporangial scarcity does not quantify lifetime sexual reproduction. Pridoli Baragwanathia also conflicts with a cited account placing abrupt leaf appearance later.

The megaphyll code conflicts with the explicit precursor interpretation. Main-axis branching is unverified; summaries disagree on the sporangial surface. Species authorship needs checking. The modelling section uses older numerical ages despite the stage-based correction, and blade dimensions remain unverified.

The Lochkovian last-stage field conflicts with reported late Lochkovian or Pragian cryptospore survivors. Conducting_tissue: absent means no water-conducting cells, not no food-conducting cells. Membership, especially Lenticulatheca and possible Culullitheca/Partitatheca, is disputed; height is inferred and older numerical ages require care.

The height note says only xylem cylinders are known, but topotypes preserve cortex; its 27 mm length is from a search summary. The modelling claim of wood without leaves or roots exceeds their unknown status. A numeric maximum of 6 contradicts 'over 6 mm'; bifacial cambium remains speculative.
The Lochkovian first stage is conservative, not demonstrated. Hedeia and Yarravia are synonymised and must not be counted independently. The generic diameter range combines two species.

The conducting_tissue state 'tracheids' compresses a mixed anatomical description. Irregular tetrads do not supply a numerical meiotic error rate. The gametophyte entry uses a proposed associated form-taxon, rather than an organically connected generation.

Branching is scored isotomous although daughter-axis equality is unstated. New York Aneurospora cf. heterodonta and later Acinosporites lindlarensis assignments are unreconciled. The card's fecundity synthesis combines independently sourced size and count observations.

height_cm and axis_diameter_mm encode thallus length and breadth. Several quantitative claims lack specimen/site identifiers or primary measurements. Spore size is attributed to a preprint, and spore aperture is unknown.

Gametophyte dominance is asserted more strongly than the unexamined associated capsule permits for quantitative life-cycle modelling. Oil-body homology and lateral inhibition are interpretations; the numerical targets concern dark-cell patterns.

The form genus may pool unrelated organisms; Gotland material discussed in the card was assigned to Nematothallopsis. Ludlow records do not all resolve the Ludfordian substage. Coprolite counts describe mixed dietary samples, not Nematothallus consumption rates.

The gametophyte entry uses a proposed associated form-taxon rather than an organic connection. The trilete state is inferred from Retusotriletes identity, not a described aperture. Enations are a comparative scoring choice, and lignification is unshown.

The modelling section strengthens inferred physiology and parent size beyond direct observations. Qusaiba-1 measurements include earliest Silurian material. Single-type Oman spore masses do not establish homospory across unknown parent plants.

The type locality conflicts between the Steytlerville index entry and the Piauí description. PBDB Rhyniaceae placement conflicts with the card's tentative Lycopsida placement. Original descriptions were unread, and genus limits against Haplostigma remain unresolved.

Gedinnian–Lochkovian equivalence was not checked; Pridoli and United States records are unverified. The modelling prose treats a hypothetical diploid Parka as non-vascular although conducting tissue is scored unknown. Reproductive-structure identity remains disputed.

The modelling section states absence of water-conducting tissue categorically, although front matter records conducting tissue as unknown and eophyte membership as possible. The diameter maximum is a group proxy; height is inferred. Stomatal presence varies between species despite the single front-matter present state.

Front-matter height bounds combine inferred sizes of different species, not a measured population range. Pseudomonopodial branching lacks preserved-apex confirmation. Heterospory is scored absent from a single reported spore type in P. dalhousii.

The online key supplies morphology without a publication year or specimen identifiers; citations therefore retain its access date. Front-matter height is branch length. Branching, venation, axillary sporangia, homospory and roots include genus/family extrapolations. The claim that measured traits exist only for congeners conflicts with species-specific key dimensions.

No species-level biological parameters are available; transferable content is restricted to occurrence coding and preservation. Lochkovian first occurrence does not encompass the expressly unexcluded Pridoli possibility. The unseen thesis limits categorical nomenclatural claims. Published informal-name listings qualify the assertion that literature databases cannot contain the name.

Sources give about 33 to 37 species; the table's 33 taxa include open nomenclature and were counted by the card author. Front-matter categorical traits compress member heterogeneity. Other-card dates are reported as inconsistent. The bibliography labels Cascales-Minana 2017, online 2018, while the text cites 2018.

The diameter minimum 56 mm is the widest dimension of the largest Rhynie fragment, not a population minimum. Branching is scored none despite the branched Schunnemunk specimen. The prose treats great standing height more confidently than the length caveat permits. The 8.83 m and 8.88 m historical lengths differ; earliest occurrences remain disputed.

The height range combines secondary reconstructions of different species. Generic architecture and monophyly remain unresolved. Species-level measurements must not be pooled, and rooting function is inferred. The card labels P. crenulatum earliest Emsian while warning that its radiometric anchor and project stage boundary do not align.

Spores are scored na only because monolete spores fall outside the vocabulary; spores are present. Height combines flora observations and one population. Blue-light and fungal-cytology experiments lack specimen provenance in the card. The single garden spore measurement is not a population range.
resolution: spore state now 'monolete' (vocabulary extended); other points open

lead: Height bounds conflate fragment length and inferred stature; axis dimensions and branching rely on abstract-level or secondary summaries. Rhineland congeners appear in a species card's locality list but do not establish its range. The proposed ghost-lineage duration depends on unresolved phylogenetic placement.

Remyophyton is the card's identified gametophyte morphotaxon, treated here as the associated generation rather than a borrowed congener proxy. Stature and diameter are unchecked secondary values. Male-biased counts lack an explained cause; inferred water-use efficiency and recolonisation do not provide rates.

The body assigns stomata to all seven plants, whereas the front matter reports observations in five. Trait notes cite Kerp 2018, while the reference is listed as Kerp 2017 with a 2018 issue date. Several aggregate trait states conceal member differences.

Kerp 2017 and Taylor et al. 2005 reverse the reported sex-specific Remyophyton heights. The height maximum of 2 cm is not a secure upper bound because Lyonophyton is described as at least 2 cm. Photosynthesis and the size ratio are interpretations or derivations.

range.last is Lochkovian although its notes allow Jiangyounia into the basal Pragian. The height maximum of 10 cm conflicts with the note that Tichavekia may exceed 10 cm. Aggregate states obscure unbranched members and taxon-specific anatomical evidence.

gametophyte.state is known despite the disputed identification. Only abstract-level morphology is available, so no numerical mechanism can be parameterised. The authors' 407-411 Ma range differs from the project's Pragian boundaries, and the dating basis was not accessed.

range.last is Pragian although its notes allow an Emsian age. The modelling summary rounds sporangial measurements; the proposals retain the more precise morphology-section values. Fragment lengths do not establish upright stature, and the genus is a shape category rather than a natural group.

Front-matter trait notes mix focal-species descriptions with Scottish cf. material and a Venezuelan species; borrowed entries identify those comparative observations, not the provenance of every categorical state. Indeterminate unrolling growth is presented as a modelling rule despite its inferential basis. Type-material dating is only moderate.

The card does not identify the species or collection site underlying the vascular-element observations. height_cm records pendent length rather than upright height. spores.state is na because monolete spores fall outside the vocabulary, despite their observed presence.
resolution: spore state now 'monolete' (vocabulary extended); other points open

lead: Rhuddanian is used as a conservative range boundary rather than a demonstrated stage assignment for the type material. The review's 419-359 Ma range differs from the card's broader account. Primary methods, specimen-level measurements and quantitative physiology are unavailable.

Aggregate tracheid, rhizome and homospory states are documented for selected members only. Wilhowia's placement is disputed within the card. Whole-plant heights are reconstructed, and the tracheid-diameter correlation spans early vascular plants rather than supplying a trimerophyte-specific hydraulic relationship.

The card supplies no collection sites or specimen identifiers for the quantitative studies. Its classical haplontic baseline remains unverified for U. zonata, and marine Codiolum interpretations differ. Species within Ulothrix are retained separately; Monostroma observations are comparative body-text evidence, not front-matter trait measurements.

The conducting-tissue entry combines Gilboa xylem evidence with cellular detail from Xinicaulis; only the latter is borrowed. Eospermatopteris is explicitly treated as part of the reconstructed whole plant. Wattieza's primary versus secondary growth mode remains unsettled.

The basal charcoal horizon has unresolved upper Ludlow versus basal Pridoli assignments. Front-matter height summarises preserved Cooksonia lengths, not complete plants; conducting tissue and spore states combine distinct member lineages.

The original hyphal interpretation is disputed by an abstract-only reinterpretation as cyanobacterial sheaths. No dimensions or exchange rates are supplied. The Pragian range is narrower than the Pragian-to-possibly-earliest-Emsian dating note.

Front matter records compression preservation, but the text says this is assumed. The taxon count, specimen counts and locality totals are incomplete; published geographic province labels also differ.

The Lochkovian first-stage entry is explicitly conservative rather than demonstrated. Silurian Yea dates and the South African identification remain disputed. The principal redescription was read through its reproduction in McSweeney (2024).

The last-stage field says Frasnian, while its note says Last = Givetian. Height combines near-complete plants with preserved axis lengths. Heterospory is coded absent despite heterosporous members in the inclusive grade; the Pridoli gap also remains unresolved.
resolution: range note relabelled 'Last = Frasnian', matching range.last

lead: The Pridoli gap conflicts with reported Z. qujingense occurrences. Conducting anatomy, complete rooting architecture and reproductive-volume estimates come from different species; they must remain separate rather than forming a synthetic genus-wide plant.
The Closterium species is specified only in the reference title. The Middle Devonian Palaeoclosterium claim is unexamined, whereas unmistakable conjugate zygospores are placed in the Carboniferous.

States that tracheids are known only from Lochkovian C. pertoni, but Morris et al. (2024, doi 10.37520/fi.2024.012) cite Ludlow Cooksonia annular thickenings (Edwards & Davies 1976, doi 10.1038/263494a0); rhyniophytoids carries the same claim. Bears on record-timing (oldest tracheids). Raised by the Sonnet card agent, 2026-10-28
resolution: Holds, with a qualification. The 1976 abstract (ORCA, Cardiff) reports a vascular plant with in situ tracheids from Whitcliffian (late Ludlow) strata of South Wales; Morris et al. 2024 describe annular thickenings in stems ending in Cooksonia-type sporangia, but Edwards 1979 tabulates 'Y-axes + tracheids' beside Cooksonia sp. and Edwards et al. 1992 say tracheids were never shown in attached axes. Cooksonia, rhyniophytoids and Tortilicaulis offaeus cards corrected 2026-10-28 (Claude Opus 5.5); attachment left open pending the full text (closed register).
